title: Granularity slider
summary: Add dimensions one by one to a view of Minutes Watched and watch the marks split, the values shrink and the aggregation decide whether the pieces add back up.
intro: Slide to add dimensions to a view of `Minutes Watched`, each on a different shelf, and switch the aggregation. Every dimension in the view, wherever it sits, adds to the level of detail: the rows are split into more, smaller groups, and the measure is computed again for each one.

copy.none: No dimension in the view: all the sessions form one group, so the view has a single mark.
copy.headers: A dimension on Rows or Columns adds headers, and Tableau computes the measure again once per member.
copy.color: "Encoding a dimension by a property on the Marks card (such as Color or Size) increases the number of marks without adding headers." Each bar splits into one segment per device.
copy.detail: Detail adds a dimension to the level of detail without colour, size or headers: more marks, smaller values, nothing new to read on the axes.
copy.marks: The number of marks can be at most the number of member combinations; combinations that have no rows draw no mark.
copy.additive: SUM is additive: the pieces add back up to the total.
copy.nonAdditive: This aggregation isn't additive: adding up the pieces doesn't give the value for the whole.
copy.sql: In SQL terms, the aggregation is the function in `SELECT SUM(minutes)`, and the dimensions in the view are the `GROUP BY` list. The slider adds columns to `GROUP BY`.
